A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Bayesian WeakS-to-Strong. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: V2 reports original SciQ classification and SLURP slot-filling experiments, including ensemble comparisons, cDPO results and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds CosmosQA results and FlyingSquid comparisons.

M1.justification: Equation (7) revises the stated token-label calculation from allocating word probability using positive-exponent confidence weights to allocating log-probability using negative-exponent weights. This changes the specified target probabilities within the retained pipeline; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: V3 Appendix D adds CosmosQA commonsense reading comprehension, reformulated as binary answer-correctness classification. This extends the classification domain while retaining SciQ and SLURP and the same two broad task types.

E2.justification: FlyingSquid is newly evaluated in the three- and five-teacher SciQ comparisons in Table 2 and the three-teacher CosmosQA comparison in Table 7. Existing single-teacher, Naive Multi-Weak and Joint Decoding comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added CosmosQA evaluation specifies 5,000 examples for weak-model training, another 5,000 for strong-model training, and 1,000 for testing, using three teachers and auxiliary-loss controls. This is an additional evaluation setup; the stated settings of the retained SciQ and SLURP experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: The probability-estimation ablation, weighting analysis, Joint Decoding teacher-quality and beam-size studies, and model-complementarity analysis are retained. V2 Appendices D–F become v3 Appendices E–G. CosmosQA adds benchmark coverage rather than a distinct ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Table 5 newly reports individual seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 outcomes alongside the existing means and standard deviations. Both versions already specify three runs; there is no reported increase in runs or new uncertainty estimator or significance test.

E6.justification: V3 adds FlyingSquid scores, CosmosQA results and individual cDPO seed results while retaining existing benchmark scores. On CosmosQA with auxiliary loss, Bayesian Multi-Weak reports accuracy 0.760, versus 0.731 for the best single-teacher configuration and 0.706 for FlyingSquid. Section 6.1 also replaces the earlier 11%/7% comparison wording with 16%/8% relative PGR differences.

T1.justification: Equation (4) corrects the teacher-specific probability and class-specific one-hot target in the EDL sum. Equation (7) changes the decomposition to log-probabilities, making the implied token-probability product preserve word probability. These are mathematical corrections; the appendix regularization derivation is retained and no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about Bayesian weak-model ensembles, extension from classification to generation, token-level supervision and cDPO. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: The explanations involving complementary weak-model errors, Bayesian fault tolerance, auxiliary supervision and Joint Decoding failures remain. The CosmosQA discussion reiterates the existing interpretation concerning uneven teacher quality. The limitations and broader-impact sections are unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 discloses equal classification ensemble weights and generation weights of (0.1, 0.3, 0.2, 0.3, 0.1), and explains averaging PGR across teachers. It replaces the promised future code release with a repository link and adds dataset access information. These are documentation and access additions, not established changes to retained experimental settings.

R1.justification: V3 adds Fu et al. (2020) for FlyingSquid and Huang et al. (2019) for CosmosQA. FlyingSquid introduces a comparison with probabilistic weak supervision, while the related-work section and broader novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized explanatory edits, adds the FlyingSquid description and CosmosQA appendix, and renumbers subsequent appendices. Author affiliations, ordering and publication headers are updated. The main narrative and section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains FlyingSquid rows, Table 5 expands to show individual seeds, and new Tables 6–7 present CosmosQA results. The asset table gains access-path information. Existing figures and ablation tables remain, with limited spacing changes and relocation.

improvement.justification: Corrected equations, an additional comparator and classification dataset, and clearer reproducibility information provide a limited net improvement. The original claims and results remain stable. A remaining reporting problem tempers the gain: CosmosQA Tables 6–7 imply GPT2-Large PGR of approximately 0.049 without auxiliary loss, whereas 0.077 is reported.
